big: A category does well for a year and money pours in. Next year it falls and money flows out. Investors in it earn less than the fund itself did. That gap is real and has a name: the behaviour gap.

lines: The fund returned 18%. Why did investors earn less?
Most of the money came in after the good run and left after the bad one. The fund's return is one thing. What its average investor earned is another.

alt: Two bars showing the fund's return above the average investor's return
caps: The fund returned 18% over the period.
Money arrived late, after most of the gain.
Some investors left during the fall.
The average investor earned less: the behaviour gap.

title: Performance chasing
stops: Chasing buys after much of the gain has happened
The behaviour gap is usually positive
Heavy category flows show what investors want
Flows show what suits every client
caps: Recent returns look vivid, so people buy late.
It is usually negative for investors.
Suitability depends on each client's risk and horizon.

opts: The gap between two funds' fees
The gap between SIP and lump sum
The gap between buy and sell prices
why: Fees are a different matter from behaviour. It does not answer what was asked.
SIP versus lump sum is a method question. The details here point elsewhere.
Buy and sell prices relate to dealing, not behaviour. That does not match this case.
It is the difference between the fund and its average investor.

q: A category tops the one-year chart. A client wants to move all her money into it. What does the RM do?
opts: Move everything today, as she asks
Check it against her risk and horizon
Refuse to discuss any category now
Predict that the category will fall
why: Acting only on recent returns is performance chasing.
Allocation should fit her risk tolerance and horizon.
Refusing to discuss it helps no one. It does not fit the facts given.
No one can predict that with confidence. It does not answer what was asked.

q: Heavy flows into a category tell the RM what?
opts: That the category will keep rising
That it is safe from losses
why: Flows do not forecast future returns.
No category is safe from losses.

q: What is the RM's best role in a hot category?
opts: Help clients stay invested in falls
Push clients into whatever is rising
Tell clients to exit after any fall
why: The aim is a fit allocation that clients can stay with.
Forecasting winners is not a reliable skill.
Pushing into what is rising is chasing.
Exiting after each fall locks in the gap.

pts: Chasing means buying what just did well, often late.
The behaviour gap is fund return less investor return.
Fit allocation to risk and horizon, so clients can stay put.
